corrections.why: NUM (Numidia/E. Algeria, i.e. the Béjaïa–Constantine hinterland) is assigned to the Zayyanid Kingdom of Tlemcen, but Tlemcen's territory lay far to the west (Oran/Tlemcen, correctly held by 'zayyanid' via ORA). The Béjaïa–Constantine region was ruled by the western (Béjaïa) branch of the Hafsid dynasty until the Ottoman conquest of 1529; the city of Béjaïa itself fell to Spain in Jan 1510 (a presidio, city-scale like Oran/Tripoli and not meant to flip cell assignment per this file's own convention). The Ottoman regions list already correctly picks up NUM starting at the 1540 slice, confirming 1512/1526 are the slices needing the fix.

Same issue as 1512: NUM (Numidia/Béjaïa-Constantine) was still under Hafsid (Béjaïa-branch) rule in 1526, not the Zayyanid Kingdom of Tlemcen — Ottoman conquest of Constantine only came in 1529, after which the file already (correctly) shows NUM as Ottoman from the 1540 slice on.

verified: Region-assignment completeness: all 7 slices (1512, 1526, 1540, 1556, 1571, 1598, 1610) assign all 122 regions exactly once, no duplicates or gaps.
Ferdinand's conquest of Iberian Navarre in 1512: the Duke of Alba's army entered July 19 and Pamplona surrendered July 25 — a genuine 'six-day campaign' as the event states.
Selim I deposed Bayezid II in April 1512 and Massimiliano Sforza was restored as Duke of Milan in Dec 1512 after the Holy League expelled France — both correct for the 1512 slice.
Cyprus/Venice/Ottoman: Venice holds CYP through 1556, contested and shown as Ottoman-controlled with Venice contestedRegions at 1571 (Famagusta fell Aug 1571) — correctly sequenced.

Rhodes → Malta: Knights Hospitaller hold DOD (Rhodes) in 1512, are landless (correctly absent) in 1526 after the 1522 siege, and hold MLT (+ TRP 1530-1540) from the 1540 slice after Charles V's 1530 grant.
Tripolitania (TRP): Hafsid-nominal in 1512/1526, Knights Hospitaller 1540 (granted 1530), Ottoman from 1551 (shown correctly from the 1556 slice) — matches the Dragut conquest date.
Baghdad (MES_S): Safavid until the Ottoman capture in Dec 1534, correctly shown as Ottoman from the 1540 slice onward.
Peace of Amasya (1555): Erivan/eastern Georgia stayed Safavid, western Georgia/Kurdistan went Ottoman — matches the file's ARM=Safavid, GEO=contested-note treatment at 1556/1571.

Treaty of Constantinople (1590): Erivan (ARM) and the Caucasus ceded to the Ottomans — matches the file correctly showing ARM as Ottoman (and Safavid entity absent from the map) at the 1598 slice, with Safavid regaining ARM only after Shah Abbas's 1603-07 reconquest (shown correctly at 1610).
Union of Lublin (1569) transferring Ukraine (UKR_W) from Lithuania to the Polish crown, and the Livonian Order's collapse (EST to Sweden, LVA to Poland-Lithuania) are both correctly timed.
Kazan (1552) and Astrakhan (1556) conquests, Muscovy→Russia id switch at the 1556 slice (post-1547 coronation), Zaporozhian Cossack Sich founding (c. 1552) — all consistent with mainstream dating.

Duchy of Prussia's 1525 secularization and Polish vassalage, Croatia's absorption into the Habsburg AUT/SVK/CRO bloc after 1540, and Sardinia/Naples/Sicily kept as separate crown-territory entities under the Aragonese/Spanish monarch throughout — all defensible and consistent.

uncertainties: Did not flag the Zayyanid/Hafsid NUM correction's exact hand-off year with more precision than 'still wrong at 1512 and 1526, already fixed by 1540' — the file has no slice between 1526 and 1540 to pin down whether the 1529 Ottoman conquest of Constantine should instead be modeled as a brief Hafsid→Ottoman transition rather than Zayyanid→Ottoman; assigning the interim to 'hafsid' is the best fit given available entities.

Considered but did not flag: Wattasid Morocco holding all of MAR (Marrakesh) in the 1512 slice despite the Saadi movement's 1511 founding in the Sous — left alone because the Saadis did not take Marrakesh city until 1524/25 per the file's own (correct) 1526 note, so Wattasid nominal control of MAR in 1512 is defensible.

Considered but did not flag the 1526 event text 'Gustav Vasa's Sweden, independent since 1523, breaks decisively from the Kalmar Union' — the formal Treaty of Malmö break was 1524, two years before this slice; left it as a retrospective event summary rather than a territorial error.
